Private equity news across North America: buyouts, fundraising, exits and investor activity in the region.

The Hong Kong-listed investment company has become 'more active' amid greater visibility around exits, managing director Gary Chan tells PEI Private Equity.

Founders who are slow in succession planning risk handing over firms their successors cannot afford to buy, according to a report from Bain & Co.

An introduction to PEI Private Equity, and why Hamilton Lane is sounding the alarm over PE's walking dead.

A surplus of managers is diluting talent pools and creating fundraising challenges, says Erik Hirsch, executive co-chairman, in the latest episode of PEI's Spotlight podcast.

The adoption of artificial intelligence is well underway for private equity firms, with cost reduction being a major focus.

In today's edition, Why the US midterms could spell trouble for private funds; Secondaries fundraising dips; Matching individual investors with UK private assets.

The $330bn New York pension system's Monte Tarbox says he is 'losing confidence' that GPs expanding into the retail market are keeping pension funds at the core of their strategic operations.

Capital raising appears poised to surpass by year-end the $580bn secured by North America-based PE funds in 2025.

As durations extend, the game has changed for investors in private equity buyout strategies, writes Wil Warren, partner and president of Lexington Partners.

Cyber risk, the need for proprietary data and the rush to finance AI are top of mind for Carlyle Group CEO Harvey Schwartz.

Is an elevated hurdle rate a good idea?
